title: Hosea: take with you words (Hosea 14:2–3)
hookLine: "Take with you words, and return unto the LORD"

cards: "Take with you words, And return unto the LORD." That's the instruction, in the 1917 Jewish translation. Not a lamb.
Not gold, or a long list of promises. Words. Hosea has spent its chapters on betrayal and hurt, on a people who kept turning away.
Now, at the very end, the way home opens, and the one thing they're told to carry costs nothing and can be the hardest to find: the right words.

teach.b: The passage opens with one Hebrew word: shuvah. Return. "Return, O Israel, unto the LORD thy God."
Jewish tradition hears in it teshuvah, the word for repentance, which means turning back, coming home.
And Hosea doesn't leave the words up to them. He gives them a script: say unto Him, forgive all iniquity, accept that which is good. Then a striking line.
The King James has: "so will we render the calves of our lips." The 1917 Jewish translation spells out the picture: "So will we render for bullocks the offering of our lips."
Bulls were once brought as offerings; here the lips take their place, and words become the offering.

Some readers hear a quiet idea that the rabbis made central after the Temple was gone: with no altar, prayer stands where the sacrifice stood. A sorry, said out loud, becomes a kind of gift. And notice the order.
Not a feeling first. Words first. Turning back often begins with a sentence that's hard to say, and saying it changes something.
Hosea knew how hard; that's why he hands them the words.

teach.h: SHABBAT SHUVAH, THE SABBATH OF RETURN.
teach.b: The chapter gives its name to a Shabbat: Shabbat Shuvah, the Sabbath of Return, between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, when Jews read this very passage in synagogue, at the season of turning back.

how: Jews read Hosea 14 as the haftarah on Shabbat Shuvah, the Sabbath between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, and teshuvah, returning, is the theme of that season.

o: the prophet who tells the people to bring words when they return
the prophet who told them to bring rams and gold to the altar
a prophet who warned them that no road home was left at all

games.q: you've done wrong and want to come back. according to Hosea 14, what do you bring?
games.why: take with you words, and return unto the LORD. and Hosea even supplies them: our lips will be our offering.

practice: Bring to mind one sorry you owe, big or small, a sharp tone, a missed call, a promise that slid, and do what Hosea does: write the script in the plainest words you can, no explanation, no defense, something like I was wrong about this, and I'm sorry.
Say it silently a few times, until it sounds like you. If you pray, you can bring the same plain words to God.

wordCard.voice: Hosea. The prophet who ends his book with a way home, and tells the people to take words with them when they return. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: return! the first word of Hosea 14:2, and the name of Shabbat Shuvah.

carryVoice: Your line: take with you words. The week ran from flesh is more vulnerable than stone, through dry bones and a healing river, to Hosea's way home. That's day eight hundred nineteen.
